# zupix

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zupix/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zupix/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedrobtz/zupix/gh-pages/badges/coverage.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zupix/actions/workflows/coverage.yaml)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

zupix reads and writes PNG, JPEG, WebP and QOI images. Each of those formats
is already readable from R, but through a system library (libpng, libjpeg,
libwebp) or ImageMagick, which has to be installed before the package can
be built from source. And images arrive from the network, from PDFs and
from users, so decoding one is parsing input nobody has checked.

zupix compiles every codec into the package and treats every file as
hostile:

* **No system library.** Installing zupix needs a C compiler and the zlib R
  is built with, nothing else. PNG, JPEG and WebP decode through
  [Wuffs](https://github.com/google/wuffs) and QOI through
  [qoi.h](https://qoiformat.org/); encoding goes through zupix's own PNG
  writer, [libjpeg-turbo](https://libjpeg-turbo.org/),
  [libwebp](https://developers.google.com/speed/webp) and qoi.h.
* **Built for hostile input.** Wuffs's decoders are memory-safe by
  construction, QOI streams are checked complete before qoi.h decodes
  them, and every size an image declares is checked against `pix_limits()`
  before anything is allocated. zupix's own metadata
  scanners are fuzzed.
* **The pixels the file holds.** No colour management, gamma or orientation
  is applied unless you ask. ICC profiles and EXIF blocks come out as raw
  bytes, and the EXIF orientation is applied only with `orient = TRUE`.
* **Familiar shapes.** Images decode to a `nativeRaster` or an array, as
  the png package returns them, at 8 or 16 bits, and the writers take the
  same shapes back.
* **A C interface for other packages.** The same codecs are available to
  C code through a registered function table.

## Installation

zupix is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zupix")
```

## Usage

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(zupix)
```

`pix_info()` reads what an image is from its header, without decoding a
pixel. It takes any number of files.

```{r}
f <- system.file("extdata", "gradient.png", package = "zupix")
pix_info(f)[c("format", "width", "height", "bits", "colour_type", "alpha")]
```

`pix_read()` decodes to a `nativeRaster` by default, ready for
`grid::grid.raster()`. Ask for `"integer"` or `"double"` to work with the
values; the shape is `height x width x channels`.

```{r}
img <- pix_read(f, as = "integer")
dim(img)
img[1:2, 1:3, 1]
```

The writers take the same shapes. Here the image goes out as a JPEG that
carries an EXIF orientation of 6, "rotate 90 degrees clockwise to display".
Reading it back returns the pixels as stored unless `orient = TRUE` says
to apply that.

```{r}
exif <- as.raw(c(0x49, 0x49, 0x2a, 0, 8, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0x12, 1, 3, 0, 1, 0,
                 0, 0, 6, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0))
jpg <- pix_write_jpeg(img, quality = 90L, exif = exif)
pix_info(jpg)$orientation
dim(pix_read(jpg, as = "integer"))
dim(pix_read(jpg, as = "integer", orient = TRUE))
```

Every size an image declares is checked before memory is allocated. A
breach is a `zupix_limit_error` that names the limit, raised before any
pixel memory exists.

```{r, error = TRUE}
pix_read(f, limits = pix_limits(max_pixels = 1000))
```

Every function starts with `pix_`, and every writer is `pix_write_` and a
format; `pix_write()` picks one from the file's extension.

## Learn more

* [Getting started with zupix](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupix/articles/zupix.html)
  covers the shapes, metadata, writing, limits and errors, calling zupix
  from C, how fast it is, and where it differs from the reference
  decoders.
* The [reference index](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zupix/reference/) lists
  every function.

## Acknowledgements

zupix is built on [Wuffs](https://github.com/google/wuffs) (The Wuffs
Authors), [libjpeg-turbo](https://libjpeg-turbo.org/),
[libwebp](https://chromium.googlesource.com/webm/libwebp) (Google) and
[qoi.h](https://github.com/phoboslab/qoi) (Dominic Szablewski), bundled under
their own licences (see `inst/COPYRIGHTS`). This software is based in part
on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.

It is tested against [PngSuite](http://www.schaik.com/pngsuite/) (Willem van
Schaik), libjpeg-turbo's and libwebp's test images and the QOI test images,
with the [png](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=png),
[jpeg](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=jpeg),
[webp](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=webp) and
[qoi](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=qoi) packages and libjpeg-turbo's
`djpeg` as reference decoders.
